::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[Need help in understanding set ordered relationship.](https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/1499375/need-help-in-understanding-set-ordered-relationship), asked by [kishoredbn](https://math.stackexchange.com/users/16119/kishoredbn) on Mathematics Stack Exchange (2015-10-27; [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/)):

> I am reading a paper, where it is said that **X** is a set ordered by relation **R**. Any subset **Y** of **X** is then ordered by the restriction of **R** to **Y**, i.e. by **R∩(YxY)**.
>
> I want to know what is meant by this notation  **R∩(YxY)**.
:::

There is nothing fancy in this restriction.  It just means that if you have a relation on $X$, and $Y \subseteq X$, then you have a relation on $Y$ too.

For example: Let $X = \mathbb{R}$ and $R$ be the less-than relation $<$.  Let $Y = \mathbb{N}$.  Then we can order $\mathbb{N}$ by the same relation.
